$comment: Rule catalog — proof obligations, dependency traceability, edge cases. Standards 6, 7, 8, 9, 20.

rules.title: Claims at proved rank enumerate their obligations
rules.description: Every claim at LEMMA rank or above carries an Obligations field, each obligation having an identifier, a statement, and a state of open or discharged.
rules.rationale: 'Complete' becomes a checkable claim about a list rather than a feeling about an argument.
rules.remediation: Add the Obligations field. A claim with genuinely nothing to enumerate writes `none`, which asserts that the author looked.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that a list exists. It cannot establish that the list is complete: a proof with four obligations and three written down passes, and nothing in a text file knows about the fourth.

rules.title: Every declared dependency resolves
rules.description: Every identifier in a Depends or Assumptions field resolves to a ledger entry or to an external reference defined in the ledger's References section.
rules.rationale: A dangling identifier means the claim rests on something the project can no longer identify, which makes the claim unevaluable.
rules.remediation: Register the missing claim, add the external reference with its citation, or correct the identifier.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact over declared edges. A proof that uses a result it never cites has an undeclared edge, and no check sees it.

rules.title: A theorem is never assumed in its own proof
rules.description: A claim appears in its own dependency closure, directly or through any chain of Depends and Assumptions edges.
rules.rationale: Direct self-reference is easy to spot. What the closure catches is the version that is not: A through B through C back to A, with a dozen pages between each step and no single place where the loop is visible.
rules.remediation: Break the cycle by finding which edge is wrong. One of the claims in the reported cycle does not actually depend on the next.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact over the declared graph. A circular argument routed through an undeclared assumption produces no cycle here, and circularity inside a single proof text is invisible to a graph search.

rules.title: A proof is never complete while obligations are open
rules.description: A claim at LEMMA rank or above has at least one obligation whose state is open.
rules.rationale: The main argument works, three side conditions were going to be routine, and the paper says the theorem is proved. This compares two fields of one ledger entry and is not a judgement about mathematics at all.
rules.remediation: Discharge the obligation and point at where, promote it to its own claim and depend on it, or lower this claim's status.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact over the obligations that were enumerated. An obligation nobody listed is not open, not discharged, and not visible.

rules.title: A counterexample search is performed and recorded
rules.description: A universally quantified claim above CONJECTURE rank carries evidence of type counterexample-search or proof.
rules.rationale: A search that never happened and a search that found nothing are different facts that get reported the same way — as silence.
rules.remediation: Run a counterexample search and record it with its scope: the range, the arithmetic, the script, and the negative result.
rules.$assuranceNote: Reads the declared evidence types. Warning-level because a claim with a complete proof does not need a search — the rule exists for the case where the proof is not there yet.

rules.title: Boundary and degenerate cases are addressed
rules.description: The empty case, the smallest cases, the trivial object, the boundary of the domain, and equality in strict inequalities are addressed rather than left implicit.
rules.rationale: Most false conjectures are false somewhere boring — at n equals zero, the empty set, or the one degenerate configuration the argument assumed away.
rules.remediation: Work through Standard 9 R1's list for this claim; each case is either excluded in the Domain field or discharged as an obligation.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Knowing which cases are degenerate for a given claim is knowing the mathematics.

rules.title: Moving the difficulty into a new lemma is not progress
rules.description: The unresolved difficulty is relocated into a newly defined lemma, and progress is claimed on the grounds that the main theorem follows from that lemma.
rules.rationale: The manoeuvre is usually not conscious. The main theorem genuinely does follow from the lemma, the derivation may be elegant, and nothing stated is false — but the hard part has acquired a name and a number, and naming a difficulty is not solving it.
rules.remediation: State why the new lemma is more tractable than the original, in specific terms. Where there is no such reason, record the decomposition as lateral and leave the target's status where it was.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. The structural half is caught by claims.status-exceeds-support — the target stays capped by its conjectural lemma. Whether the new lemma is the original difficulty wearing a hat, or a genuine decomposition, needs a mathematician.

rules.title: Clearly and obviously never conceal an obligation
rules.description: A triviality marker — clearly, obviously, trivially, it is well known that, one easily sees — stands in for a nontrivial proof obligation that is never enumerated.
rules.rationale: The prose dual of hiding an assumption: nothing false is stated, and a real obligation is skipped. The words are not prohibited; using them to replace an argument rather than abbreviate one is.
rules.remediation: Enumerate what the marker covers as an obligation, then discharge it — a citation is a perfectly good discharge.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Finding the words is trivial and useless; deciding whether what they cover is genuinely routine is the mathematics.

rules.title: Existence is never presented as construction
rules.description: A nonconstructive existence result is stated or used as though an explicit object, algorithm, or bound had been exhibited.
rules.rationale: Downstream work frequently needs the object rather than its existence, and an ineffective bound cannot certify any particular case — which is what such bounds are most often used for.
rules.remediation: State the claim as nonconstructive, and where a construction is needed, record that as a separate open claim.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Whether a proof is constructive is a property of the argument.

rules.title: Induction has a base case and a uniform step
rules.description: An induction omits its base case, uses a base case that does not establish the claimed starting point, or uses a step that fails for small values of the index.
rules.rationale: The all-horses-are-the-same-colour shape: the step is valid for every large n and fails at the one small case that connects the argument to its base.
rules.remediation: Enumerate the base case and the uniformity of the step as separate obligations and discharge each, checking the step explicitly at the smallest values.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Established by a reviewer, or by formalising the induction, which cannot be completed with a missing base case.
